title: Morph Cube Animation Sequencer on Coffee Mat Stage
description: A coffee mat serves as a stage platform where an AnimatedMorphCube performs choreographed morph sequences. The user builds a timeline of morph keyframes by clicking control points, adjusts playback speed and easing per segment, and can undo/redo edits. A total animation energy budget constrains how many morph transitions can be queued, enforcing conservation of animation resources across the timeline.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads coffeemat.glb and AnimatedMorphCube.glb using GLTFLoader. Place the coffee mat flat at the origin as a stage platform. Position the AnimatedMorphCube centered on top of the mat, scaled appropriately. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,5) looking at the origin, with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.4) and a directional light from (2,4,3). Implement these interactions: 1) A timeline bar at the bottom of the screen with 8 slots. Clicking a slot opens a dropdown to assign one of 4 morph target states (rest, stretch, squash, twist) mapped to the cube's morph target influences. 2) Each filled slot consumes energy points (rest=0, stretch=2, squash=2, twist=3) from a total budget of 12 points displayed as a bar. This conservation law prevents overfilling the timeline. 3) Right-clicking a filled slot cycles its easing (linear, easeIn, easeOut) shown by a colored border. 4) A speed slider (0.5x-2x) globally scales playback duration. 5) A Play button animates the cube through the sequenced morph states in order, interpolating morph target influences with the chosen easing per segment, while the coffee mat subtly pulses emissive glow in sync with each transition. 6) Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) for all slot assignments and easing changes, maintaining a history stack of at least 15 states. 7) A Clear All button resets the timeline and restores full energy. 8) During playback, a progress indicator highlights the active slot. Display the energy budget numerically and as a colored bar that transitions from green to red as budget depletes. All UI uses HTML/CSS overlays.
